metadata.archetype_justification: The application connects directly to a Microsoft Access database and performs INSERT operations via ADO. It owns persistent state (customer records) and exposes CRUD operations on business entities. No message queues, no downstream service calls, no event processing detected.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.15 yields Not Ready band (< 1.5) but 11 High findings (< 12 threshold) maps to Remediation Required tier. The divergence occurs because the count-based system only counts core-question score-1 findings as High, while the numeric score reflects all 33 evaluated questions scoring near 1.0. The count-based tier is authoritative.

findings.title: Managed Compute — No cloud compute exists
findings.description: All compute is a Win32 desktop EXE (VB6 runtime) running on individual Windows laptops. The server is a single Windows file server hosting an SMB share. No cloud compute, no managed services.
findings.gap: No managed compute of any kind. No ECS, EKS, Lambda, Fargate, or EC2.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the application as a web service deployed on managed compute (ECS Fargate or Lambda).

findings.title: Managed Databases — All databases self-managed
findings.description: Primary database is Microsoft Access 2003 (.mdb) on an SMB file share. Reporting database is SQL Server 2012 synced nightly via DTS/SSIS. Both self-managed, on-premises.
findings.gap: All databases self-managed with no managed database services. Monthly data corruption from concurrent writes.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS for data migration and AWS SCT for schema conversion.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — No orchestration service
findings.description: The nightly DTS/SSIS data sync is a multi-step workflow with no dedicated orchestration service. All workflow logic is in the SSIS package — a proprietary, unversioned construct.
findings.gap: No orchestration — DTS/SSIS nightly sync is hardcoded with no managed orchestration, no retry logic visibility.
findings.recommendation: Use AWS Step Functions for the data sync workflow when rebuilding.

findings.title: Async Messaging and Streaming — No messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure exists. Desktop app writes directly to Access DB synchronously. State changes have no event propagation — only a nightly batch DTS/SSIS job.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries. Customer records propagated only via nightly batch causing 24-hour data staleness.
findings.recommendation: Introduce EventBridge or SQS for event-driven state propagation when rebuilding.

findings.title: Network Security — No network isolation
findings.description: No VPC, no cloud networking, no network segmentation. Database is on an open SMB file share accessible to anyone on the corporate network.
findings.gap: No network isolation. Access .mdb accessible to anyone with a mapped drive.
findings.recommendation: Deploy database in a private subnet within a VPC when migrating to AWS. Use security groups with least-privilege rules.

findings.title: API Entry Point — No gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API gateway, no load balancer, no managed entry point. Desktop application connects directly to the database file share.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway or load balancer.
findings.recommendation: Use API Gateway as the entry point with throttling, request validation, and authentication when rebuilding.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — No scaling capability
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Single static file server. Access database cannot handle concurrent writes (monthly corruption).
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity statically provisioned.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling on both compute and database layers when migrating to managed services.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — No backup configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration found. Access .mdb on file share has no documented backup strategy. Monthly corruption with no recovery procedures.
findings.gap: No backup configuration; no restore procedure documented.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups with 7+ day retention and PITR when migrating to Aurora.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — No IaC exists
findings.description: Zero IaC. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or any infrastructure-as-code. All infrastructure is manually provisioned.
findings.gap: No IaC — all infrastructure created manually (ClickOps / physical hardware).
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in Terraform or AWS CDK when migrating to AWS.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — No pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. No GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CodeBuild. Application compiled on one developer's machine.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments manual. Single developer builds and distributes by hand.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline using AWS CodePipeline + CodeBuild for the replacement application.

findings.title: Programming Languages — VB6 (unsupported, no AWS SDK)
findings.description: Visual Basic 6.0 — unsupported since 2008. No AWS SDK, no cloud-native tooling, no modern framework ecosystem.
findings.gap: Language with no AWS SDK and no cloud-native tooling. Cannot integrate with modern AWS services.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in TypeScript/Node.js or Python for cloud-native development with full AWS SDK support.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — Tightly-coupled monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled desktop monolith. Single VB6 form handles UI, business logic, and data access. No separation of concerns, no module boundaries.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with no clear module boundaries, pervasive shared state.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild with clear separation of concerns. See Decomposition Strategy section.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — All synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous ADO calls to Access database. No inter-service communication, no async patterns. State changes not propagated in real-time. Archetype is stateful-crud — async should be used for cross-service state propagation.
findings.gap: All communication synchronous with no async patterns for a stateful-crud service.
findings.recommendation: Implement event-driven state propagation using EventBridge or SNS when rebuilding.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — All synchronous
findings.description: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. Nightly DTS/SSIS batch sync has no status polling, no callbacks, no timeout handling. Archetype is stateful-crud — long-running operations should be async with status polling.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration. No async job processing.
findings.recommendation: Implement long-running operations as async jobs with Step Functions or SQS workers.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — No API exists
findings.description: No API exists. Desktop EXE connects directly to database. No REST API, no versioning strategy, no API contract.
findings.gap: No versioning — no API contract exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning from day one when rebuilding as a web service (URL path: /v1/customers).

findings.title: Service Discovery — All endpoints hardcoded
findings.description: All service endpoints hardcoded in source code. Database path S:\CRM\sales.mdb is a hardcoded constant.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded. Changing database location requires recompiling the EXE.
findings.recommendation: Externalize configuration into environment variables or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — Data on inaccessible file share
findings.description: All data stored on a local SMB file share (S:\CRM\sales.mdb). No cloud accessibility, no parsing pipeline, no search capability.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems and inaccessible storage.
findings.recommendation: Migrate structured data to Aurora PostgreSQL. Use S3 for any unstructured documents.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — Scattered raw ADO calls
findings.description: Raw ADO connection management and string-concatenated SQL directly in UI event handlers. No repository pattern, no DAO, no abstraction.
findings.gap: Database queries scattered in UI code with no pattern.
findings.recommendation: Implement a repository/data access layer pattern with an ORM when rebuilding.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL — Both engines past EOL
findings.description: Access 2003 (EOL 2009) and SQL Server 2012 (EOL July 2022). Both unsupported with no security patches.
findings.gap: Engines at or past EOL detected. Both databases unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Aurora PostgreSQL 15+ as a supported managed engine. Use AWS SCT and DMS.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — No encryption configured
findings.description: No encryption at rest. Access .mdb stored unencrypted on SMB file share. Jet OLEDB Database Password is trivially bypassable obfuscation, not encryption.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Customer data in plaintext on file share.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key when migrating to Aurora.

findings.title: API Authentication — No authentication exists
findings.description: No authentication layer. Application relies solely on Windows file share permissions. No OAuth2, no JWT, no user-level authentication.
findings.gap: No API authentication — access uncontrolled beyond network file share permissions.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT authentication via Amazon Cognito when rebuilding.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — No IdP integration
findings.description: No centralized identity provider. Application identifies users via Environ("USERNAME") with no authentication, no SSO, no IdP.
findings.gap: No authentication at all — no IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with Amazon Cognito and enable SSO with organizational identity provider.

findings.title: Secrets Management — Plaintext credentials in source code
findings.description: Database password hardcoded: Private Const DB_PW As String = "crm2005pw" in frmCustomer.frm. Connection string with password compiled into the EXE.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in source code. Deployment-blocking security issue.
findings.recommendation: Rotate password immediately. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation when rebuilding.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — No patching strategy
findings.description: VB6 runtime is unsupported (no patches available). No vulnerability scanning, no hardened images, no patching process.
findings.gap: No patching strategy; no vulnerability scanning. Runtime unsupported.
findings.recommendation: Use managed compute (Fargate, Lambda) which handles OS patching automatically when migrating.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — No security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists. SQL injection vulnerability undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. Pipeline has no security validation (no pipeline exists).
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST, dependency scanning, and container scanning into CI/CD from day one.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — No tracing or observability
findings.description: No distributed tracing. On Error Resume Next suppresses all error information. No logging, no telemetry, no trace IDs.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing. Errors actively suppressed.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry and AWS X-Ray from day one when rebuilding.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — No SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLOs. Monthly data corruption accepted as normal rather than tracked as SLO violation.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for the CRM service (availability, latency, error rate) when rebuilding.

findings.title: Business Metrics — No metrics of any kind
findings.description: No custom metrics. No business metrics, no infrastructure metrics, no CloudWatch integration.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no visibility into business outcomes or system health.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics alongside infrastructure metrics to CloudWatch when rebuilding.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — No alerting
findings.description: No alerting configured. No anomaly detection, no static threshold alarms. Failures discovered by users.
findings.gap: No alerting configured. System failures discovered by end users.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection when rebuilding.

findings.title: Integration Testing — No automated tests
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. Zero test coverage. README states 'No tests, no build server.'
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests from day one. Test critical workflows in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — No runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks, no incident response automation, no self-healing. Monthly data corruption handled ad hoc.
findings.gap: No runbooks — incident response entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents. Implement automated remediation with SSM Automation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — No monitoring assets exist
findings.description: No observability ownership. No dashboards, no alarms, no CODEOWNERS. Zero monitoring assets to own.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Establish per-service dashboards and alarms with named owners when rebuilding.

findings.title: Resource Tagging Governance — No AWS resources exist
findings.description: No AWS resources exist, therefore no resource tagging. No tagging strategy, no cost allocation.
findings.gap: No tags — no AWS resources exist to tag.
findings.recommendation: Implement tagging standard from day one when provisioning AWS infrastructure.
